description:
Guincho Fortress sits directly on the Atlantic coast west of Lisbon, within the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, close to Cabo da Roca — one of the westernmost points of continental Europe. Built in the 17th century as a coastal fortification defending the approach to Lisbon, it is a fort rather than a castle in the usual sense: a low, thick-walled military structure designed to mount cannon against seaborne threats, not a noble or royal residence. Two large cannons still flank its entrance, a direct physical reminder of the building's original purpose.

The fortress was converted into a hotel in the late 1990s, and today it is a member of Relais & Châteaux, the international association of independently owned luxury hotels and restaurants known for prioritising character and setting over chain-hotel uniformity. Guincho Fortress fits that model closely: a genuinely historic military structure, on a dramatic stretch of Atlantic coastline, run as a small, design-conscious property rather than a large resort.

The hotel's restaurant, under chef Gil Fernandes, holds a Michelin star for cooking built around locally sourced, ocean-driven modern Portuguese ingredients — a serious culinary destination in its own right, set inside a panoramic room within the former military fortification, looking directly onto the Atlantic and toward Cabo da Roca. The restaurant's reputation is part of what distinguishes Guincho Fortress from Portugal's more historically grand castle-hotels: the draw here is as much about the coastline and the kitchen as about the building's military past.

The 27 rooms, suites and villas are arranged across the ground and first floors of the fortification, most of them facing the Atlantic. This is, deliberately, not a medieval castle experience — the architecture and the setting are those of a 17th-century coastal fort on one of Europe's great windswept headlands, and the hotel's own identity leans into that fact rather than away from it.
history: Guincho Fortress was built in the 17th century as a coastal fortification defending the Atlantic approach to Lisbon, part of a wider system of coastal defences along this stretch of the Portuguese coast. It was converted into a hotel in the late 1990s and is now a member of Relais & Châteaux; its restaurant, under chef Gil Fernandes, holds a Michelin star.

faqs.question: Is Guincho Fortress a medieval castle?
faqs.answer: No — it is a 17th-century coastal fortification, built to defend the Atlantic approach to Lisbon, not a medieval castle. It was converted into a hotel in the late 1990s and is now a Relais & Châteaux property.

faqs.question: Does Guincho Fortress have a Michelin-starred restaurant?
faqs.answer: Yes — the hotel's restaurant, led by chef Gil Fernandes, holds a Michelin star for its locally sourced, ocean-driven modern Portuguese cooking, served in a panoramic room within the fortification looking onto the Atlantic.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** On the Guincho coast of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, in Cascais, west of Lisbon; Lisbon airport is about 60 minutes away by road, according to the hotel. Free parking and an airport transfer service are available.

**Rooms & rates:** 27 rooms from approx. €250/night (this starting rate is low-confidence — the hotel does not publish a fixed rate; confirm current pricing before booking), all within the fortress, from ground-floor Classic rooms to first-floor Junior Suites with ocean-facing balconies.

**On-site:** Gastronomic restaurant with a Michelin star, a more casual restaurant with ocean views, a bar, and beach-front access; bicycles are free to use.

**Good to know:** This is a 17th-century coastal fortification rather than a medieval castle, and the hotel is best known for its location on the Atlantic and for its restaurant. Ground-floor Classic rooms have only partial views through small fortress windows, so upper-floor rooms are better for sea views.

**Combine with:** Cabo da Roca and the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park on the doorstep, [Pena Palace](/castles/portugal/pena-palace), [Castle of the Moors](/castles/portugal/castle-of-the-moors), [Quinta da Regaleira](/castles/portugal/quinta-da-regaleira) and [Seteais Palace](/castles/portugal/seteais-palace) in Sintra, within a short drive.
